xPosts.author: Alex Finn
xPosts.text: Google Gemini Carbon is the best model right now. It regularly changes the way I think; feels forward-looking and novel rather than averaging training data. Best tested via conversation on real hard problems, not one-shot demos.

xPosts.author: Alex Finn
xPosts.text: The new Google Gemini models are the best AI models out there right now. Yes, better than Fable and Astra. Completely different training feel; novel perspectives. Harnesses still lag, but intelligence and taste are there. Carbon is Fable-class, Neon Opus-class.

xPosts.author: Elon Musk
xPosts.text: You can create an entire company made of Grok Bots! (quoting user who wakes up to Bot having opened, tested, and merged multiple PRs).

xPosts.author: Elon Musk
xPosts.text: “Grok 4.8” is currently several different model variants in beta. We’re not yet sure which of the variants will go to wide release.

xPosts.author: Elon Musk
xPosts.text: Treat Grok @Bot like a really smart employee (quoting detailed guide on automating with Bot).

xPosts.author: Alex Finn
xPosts.text: Something is going on at Google. Released new frontier models four times in less than a month, each a major improvement. Carbon is the most intelligent model I’ve ever used; trained differently, novel insights.

xPosts.author: Elon Musk
xPosts.text: Grok @Bot can do your accounting (quoting SpaceXSI five Bots on full-time order-to-cash roles).

xPosts.author: Alex Finn
xPosts.text: Ran ChatGPT Astra 6.2 on my benchmark: 312.7/500, Fable 5.2 beat by 0.3. But Astra finished in 1/3 time, 1/3 price, 1/4 tokens. Efficiency matters.

xPosts.author: Alex Finn
xPosts.text: Testing GPT-6.2 Astra: good, better than Astra 6 at better cost, incredible at computer use, efficient. Not matching Fable 5.2 yet; test yourself against own workflows.

xPosts.author: Alex Finn
xPosts.text: Sped up AI coding 20x: have Fable 5.2 ask as many questions as needed for full plan, then create detailed Linear issues (40+), then iterate 'work on next'.

xPosts.author: Elon Musk
xPosts.text: Grok @Bot can do almost anything (quoting Starship Flight 15 highlight reel made by Bot: download livestream, select moments, edit, effects, music).

xPosts.author: SpaceX Super Intelligence
xPosts.text: Introducing Grok Bot 1.0. Bots can be shared and are more collaborative and capable than ever.

xPosts.author: Alex Finn
xPosts.text: MASSIVE. Grok Bot 1.0 just dropped (everything before was beta). Features: Team Bots for multiplayer, join video calls and act, more proactive, better self-improvement/memory, significantly better browser use.

briefs.title: Grok 4.8 remains multi-variant beta; Bot positioned as company-scale workforce; AA v5 led by Fable 5.2 with Gemini qualitative praise
points: Musk (Nov 19): “Grok 4.8” is currently several different model variants in beta. We’re not yet sure which of the variants will go to wide release. Soft Bot trials reported by some users earlier; no public API model ID, price, or independent AA scores. 4.7 remains flagship ($2/$6, 500k, watermark opt-in).

Grok Bot 1.0: Musk (Nov 19) said “You can create an entire company made of Grok Bots!” quoting a user whose Bot opened, tested, and merged PRs overnight. Continues to highlight treating Bot like a smart employee, accounting order-to-cash deployments (company-reported time savings), phone calls, and meeting joins.

AA Intelligence Index v5 (Artificial Analysis as of Nov 20): Claude Fable 5.2 (max) 65 leader; GPT-6.2 Astra (max) 62; Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh) 61; Gemini 4 Carbon (high) 60; Claude Opus 5.5 (max) 59; GPT-6.2 Sol (max) 57; Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) 55; Grok 4.7 (xhigh) 35. Pricing for most flagships stable; Gemini intro rates end Dec 1.

Alex Finn (practitioner, Nov 18–20): Calls Gemini Carbon the best model right now for novel, forward-looking thinking that changes how he approaches problems (better qualitative feel than Fable/Astra). Notes Google released multiple frontier models rapidly; harnesses lag but intelligence/taste stand out. Separate earlier notes on Astra 6.2 efficiency (1/3 time/price of Fable on his benchmark).
briefs.assumption: Grok 4.8 remains unconfirmed for wide release or API; soft Bot access is limited and variant-specific. Accounting and overnight PR claims are user/company-reported with limited independent scale verification. AA scores are from Artificial Analysis leaderboard; effort settings affect exact numbers. Qualitative “best” claims are practitioner opinion.

briefs.title: Grok Bot accounting deployments highlighted; 4.8 rollout unconfirmed; AA v5 led by Fable 5.2 with GPT-6.2 Astra rising
points: SpaceXSI (Nov 16 blog + @bot Nov 17): Five specialized Grok Bots now full-time on accounting order-to-cash (Provisioning, Billing, Billing Support, Cash Applications, Collections). Company-reported results: invoicing from ~24h to minutes; Billing Support frees ~8h/day; payment matching from 3-4h to ~30min. Estimate: would otherwise require more than doubling headcount. Musk (Nov 18): 'Grok @Bot can do your accounting' and 'can save you millions in corporate expenses' (research expenditures, call suppliers).

Grok 4.8: Still no public confirmation of soft Bot rollout or API model ID/price as of Nov 18. Musk (Nov 10) said pre-train done, now in RL on rewritten C/C++ stack, soft Bot rollout planned that week. 4.7 remains flagship ($2/$6, 500k, watermark opt-in).

AA Intelligence Index v5 (as of Nov 18): Claude Fable 5.2 (max) 64.6 leader; GPT-6.2 Astra (max) 62.1; Gemini 4 Carbon (high) 60; Claude Opus 5.5 (max) 59.1; GPT-6.2 Sol (max) 57.3; Grok 4.7 (xhigh) 35.5. Pricing for flagships largely unchanged; GPT-6.2 variants newly ranked.

Alex Finn (practitioner, Nov 16–18): Astra 6.2 scored 312.7/500 on his benchmark (Fable 5.2 +0.3) but finished in 1/3 time, 1/3 price, 1/4 tokens; calls it efficient with strong computer use. Separate workflow: Fable 5.2 asks 100+ questions for detailed plan + Linear issues (40+), then Claude Code iterates. Notes mixed X reaction to 6.2; recommends own testing.
briefs.assumption: Accounting Bot results and savings are company-reported; independent verification of scale and unit economics limited. Grok 4.8 soft Bot rollout remains unconfirmed as live with no independent AA scores or public model card. AA scores vary slightly by tracker and effort setting.

briefs.title: API text watermark flipped to opt-in; Grok Bot demos video edit and phone calls; 4.8 still unconfirmed
points: SpaceXSI docs (as of Nov 16): Text watermarking is off by default. Team admins can turn it on per model in Console. Applies to grok-4.7/4.6/4.5/4.3 and 4.20 variants. Audio voice still watermarked by default. Musk (Nov 15): 'Text watermarking with Grok is only on where the law requires it or a user asks for it.'

Grok Bot practical use: Musk (Nov 16) quoted a user who had Bot download a 23-hour Starship livestream, select highlights, edit, add effects/music. Separate highlight of Bot making phone calls (rebooking example, AI disclosure, hold music, hotel/meals). Continues to emphasize 'Grok @Bot can do almost anything.'

Alex Finn (practitioner, Nov 15–16): Detailed 6-step workflow for using latest tools — reverse prompt Fable 5.2 for project ideas, build with Claude Code + Opus 5.5, automate remaining with Grok Bot, stay above 50% of limits, build public platform. Separate note on Qwen4-Max (API) as strong open-direction competitor.

Grok 4.8: Still no public API model ID, price, or confirmed live soft Bot rollout as of Nov 16. Musk (Nov 10) said pre-train done, in RL on new C/C++ stack, soft Bot rollout planned that week. 4.7 remains flagship ($2/$6, 500k).

AA Intelligence Index v5 (latest independent): Claude Fable 5.2 (max) ~64.6 leader; Gemini 4 Carbon (high) 60; Claude Opus 5.5 (max) ~59.1; GPT-6 Astra (max) ~56.9; GPT-6.1 Sol / Sonnet 5.5 ~54–55; Grok 4.7 ~35.5 (or lower in some trackers). Pricing unchanged for flagships.
briefs.assumption: Grok 4.8 soft Bot rollout remains unconfirmed as live with no independent AA scores or public model card. Watermark opt-in change is documented; legal residual requirements may still apply in some jurisdictions. Bot phone/video demos are user-reported or staged in some cases; unit economics of always-on agents still under prior cost pressure.

briefs.title: Grok Bot 1.0 ships with Team Bots, meeting joins, and Mac local access; 4.8 soft rollout still pending confirmation
points: SpaceXSI (Nov 11): Introduced Grok Bot 1.0. Bots can be shared (Team Bots) and are more collaborative. Features include joining Google Meet/Zoom/Teams calls (answer in chat, send summaries), more proactive behavior, better self-improvement/memory of team workflows, and significantly improved browser use.

Grok Bot on Mac (Nov 12–13): Can now access Messages, Mail, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Location, and Contacts. Musk highlighted real-world use (Maye Musk: Bot moved 2000 Dropbox photos in 5 minutes after offering to do it).

Alex Finn (practitioner, Nov 11–13): Called 1.0 massive (prior was beta); listed multiplayer Team Bots, call joining/action, proactivity, better browser. Separate post: download Bot and have autonomous revenue army by night; his made $1,800. Zero programming required.

Musk (Nov 10): Pre-training done for Grok 4.8; now in RL with evals climbing. Soft rollout to Bot users later that week. Entire stack rewritten from JAX/SGLang to C/C++. 'Will bear no resemblance to 4.7.' Foundations right; not yet incredible. As of Nov 13, no confirmed public live status or independent AA score.

AA Intelligence Index v5 (latest): Fable 5.2 ~64.6 (leader, $8/$40), Gemini 4 Carbon 60 ($2/$10 intro), Opus 5.5 ~59.1 ($4/$20), Astra ~56.9 ($10/$50), Sol ~54.6 ($2/$10), Grok 4.7 ~35.5 ($2/$6). No change in Grok ranking.
briefs.assumption: Grok 4.8 soft Bot rollout was planned for the week of Nov 10 but remains unconfirmed as live with no public AA scores or API identifier. Bot 1.0 usage economics and weekly limits still under prior cost pressure. Team Bot and meeting features depend on plan tier.
